record.paper_title: Global results on rational systems in the plane, part 1
record.original_question: For the 595 special cases of the nonnegative-parameter planar rational system x_{n+1} = (a1 + b1 x_n + g1 y_n)/(A1 + B1 x_n + C1 y_n), y_{n+1} = (a2 + b2 x_n + g2 y_n)/(A2 + B2 x_n + C2 y_n), with nonnegative initial conditions and positive denominators, that are reducible to Riccati difference equations with variable coefficients, determine their boundedness behavior, their periodic behavior, and their global stability behavior.

evidence.quote: with nonnegative parameters and with arbitrary nonnegative initial conditions such that the denominators are always positive.
Open Problem 2.1. Determine the boundedness character, the periodic nature, and the global stability behaviour of the 595 special cases

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the planar system of rational difference equations
\[ x_{n+1} = \frac{\alpha_1 + \beta_1 x_n + \gamma_1 y_n}{A_1 + B_1 x_n + C_1 y_n}, \qquad y_{n+1} = \frac{\alpha_2 + \beta_2 x_n + \gamma_2 y_n}{A_2 + B_2 x_n + C_2 y_n}, \qquad n = 0,1,2,\ldots, \]
where all twelve parameters \(\alpha_i, \beta_i, \gamma_i, A_i, B_i, C_i\) (\(i=1,2\)) are nonnegative real numbers, and the initial condition \((x_0, y_0)\) is nonnegative and chosen so that the denominators remain positive for all \(n \ge 0\).

By normalizing one nonzero parameter in each equation to 1 and by considering all possible patterns of zero/nonzero parameters, one obtains finitely many special cases of this family. Among these, identify the subfamily consisting of those special cases for which, after a suitable change of variables, the system reduces to a (possibly variable-coefficient) Riccati difference equation
\[ z_{n+1} = \frac{a_n + b_n z_n}{c_n + d_n z_n}. \]
There are exactly 595 such Riccati-reducible special cases. For each of these 595 special cases, determine:

(a) the boundedness character of all solutions with admissible nonnegative initial conditions (i.e., for which parameter values are all solutions bounded, and for which do unbounded solutions exist);

(b) the periodic nature of solutions (existence, periods, and structure of periodic solutions);

(c) the global asymptotic stability behavior of equilibria (local stability, global attractivity, and global asymptotic stability on the admissible set of initial conditions).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem concerning the comprehensive classification of dynamical behavior (boundedness, periodicity, global stability) of 595 Riccati-reducible planar rational systems. Web searches did not turn up any subsequent paper resolving the entire family; only partial results on individual special cases of planar rational systems by Camouzis, Ladas and collaborators appear in the literature. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of Third-Order Rational Difference Equations with Open Problems and Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph by Camouzis and Ladas posing many open problems on rational difference equations and systems, including classification of special cases.
status_evidence.claim: The general program of classifying boundedness, periodicity, and stability for special cases of rational systems is posed as a collection of open problems.

status_evidence.title: When does local asymptotic stability imply global attractivity in rational equations?
status_evidence.snippet: Studies global attractivity in special cases of rational equations; only partial progress on the broad classification program.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results on individual special cases are available.
